resources.string: Sends you to Doomscroll Killer\'s distraction-free feed whenever the official Instagram app opens. This service only knows WHEN Instagram opens: it cannot read your screen, and nothing is sent anywhere.
Instagram, without the endless scroll. Keep what matters: the people you follow and your messages.
Your feed opens on \"Following\", newest first. No algorithm.
No Reels, no Explore, no ads
Removed before they even appear: nothing to scroll past.
Messages and activity arrive as usual and open here.
Doomscroll Killer shows instagram.com in a protected view and strips out everything built to keep you scrolling.
The official Instagram app stays installed, out of sight, only to receive notifications. If it opens, you are sent back here.
Private by design: no account, no server, no tracking. Your login stays on your phone.
Open source (GPL-3.0): anyone can check what it does.
A few permissions so the redirect and notifications work. You can change them later in Settings.

You now have two icons: \"Insta\" opens your feed, \"Doomscroll Killer\" holds these settings. Log in to Instagram once in Insta, then hide the official Instagram app\'s icon so you never open it by habit.
Accessibility service that sends you here whenever Instagram opens.
Your phone stopped it. Turn it off and on again in Accessibility settings.
Switch greyed out? Open App info → ⋮ (top right) → \"Allow restricted settings\", then try again.
Lets Doomscroll Killer take over Instagram\'s notifications.
Allows Doomscroll Killer to display them.
Stops your phone from putting the redirect to sleep.
The feed works without it. Install it (and hide its icon) only if you want notifications.

Doomscroll Killer uses Android\'s accessibility service for one thing: noticing when the official Instagram app opens, so it can send you to the distraction-free feed instead.\n\nIt cannot read what is on your screen, it only listens to Instagram, and nothing ever leaves your phone.
1. Tap \"Downloaded apps\".\n2. Tap \"Doomscroll Killer – Instagram redirect\".\n3. Turn it on, then come back with the Back button.
1. Tap \"Installed apps\".\n2. Tap \"Doomscroll Killer – Instagram redirect\".\n3. Turn it on, then come back with the Back button.
1. Open \"Downloaded apps\" (it may be called \"Installed apps\" or \"Installed services\").\n2. Tap \"Doomscroll Killer – Instagram redirect\".\n3. Turn it on, then come back with the Back button.

• Settings → Apps → Doomscroll Killer AND Instagram: turn on Autostart, set Battery saver to \"No restrictions\".\n• Lock Doomscroll Killer in Recents (long-press its card → lock icon) so it is not cleared.\n• Hide Instagram\'s icon: Security app → App lock → ⚙ → Hidden apps.
• Settings → Battery → Background usage limits: add Doomscroll Killer and Instagram to \"Never sleeping apps\".\n• Hide Instagram\'s icon: Home screen settings → Hide apps on Home and Apps screens.
• Settings → Battery → App launch: set Doomscroll Killer and Instagram to \"Manage manually\" with everything allowed.\n• Hide Instagram\'s icon by moving it to a folder, or use PrivateSpace.
• Settings → Battery → Battery optimization: set Doomscroll Killer and Instagram to \"Don\'t optimize\".\n• Hide Instagram\'s icon: open the app drawer → ⋮ → Hidden space.
• Settings → Battery → App battery management: allow background activity and auto-launch for Doomscroll Killer and Instagram.\n• Hide Instagram\'s icon: Settings → Privacy → Hide apps.
• Settings → Battery → Background power consumption: allow high usage for Doomscroll Killer and Instagram.\n• Hide Instagram\'s icon by moving it to a folder.
• Remove Instagram\'s icon from your home screen (long-press → Remove, not Uninstall) or put it in a folder: it stays installed for notifications.
Some protections are off. Tap to fix.
Check your connection and try again.

Instagram notifications show up here and open the right conversation.
Your feed, without the doomscroll. Also on your home screen.
Log out of Instagram in Doomscroll Killer? You will need to log in again.
Instagram changed something? Open an issue.
No account, no server, no analytics. Internet is only used to load instagram.com.
Saves page captures to update the filtering rules. Uses a bit more battery.
No capture yet. Turn on developer mode, then browse the feed: a capture of the page is saved every few seconds.
